confidence_notes: FX is the latest RBA observation found by search (18 Nov 2026). Food and beer anchors come from one search of crowdsourced Cairo price indexes, which put a cappuccino at about 68-84 EGP, a domestic beer at about 72-100 EGP, an inexpensive meal at about 162 EGP, and a mid-range meal for two at about 650 EGP. Those EGP figures were converted to USD with an implied rate of roughly 50 EGP per USD, which is my own assumption and not a sourced rate. Restaurant beer in a licensed venue is likely pricier than the crowdsourced pint, so I set it higher. Cocktail and wine were not searched. I estimated them from the local relationship to beer, since alcohol is taxed heavily and sold only in licensed venues, so both are uncertain. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates, not live listing checks, and they carry the most uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: Cairo is compared with other low-cost North African and Middle Eastern tourist cities, with Egyptian-pound price levels taken from crowdsourced Cairo indexes. Hotel-venue drink prices were used to bound the upper end for beer, cocktails and wine.
